preconditions.description: The input must be a string.

postconditions.description: The function must return one of the specified outcomes based on the input string.

postconditions.expression: (any(w in input.lower() for w in ['water', 'wet', 'wash']) and any(p in input.lower() for p in ['i don\'t know', 'slime'])) == (return_value == 'sludge')
postconditions.description: If both conditions for water and slime are met, the function must return 'sludge'.

postconditions.expression: (any(w in input.lower() for w in ['water', 'wet', 'wash']) and not any(p in input.lower() for p in ['i don\'t know', 'slime'])) == (return_value == 'water')
postconditions.description: If only the condition for water is met, the function must return 'water'.

postconditions.expression: (not any(w in input.lower() for w in ['water', 'wet', 'wash']) and any(p in input.lower() for p in ['i don\'t know', 'slime'])) == (return_value == 'slime')
postconditions.description: If only the condition for slime is met, the function must return 'slime'.

postconditions.expression: (not any(w in input.lower() for w in ['water', 'wet', 'wash']) and not any(p in input.lower() for p in ['i don\'t know', 'slime'])) == (return_value == 'air')
postconditions.description: If neither condition is met, the function must return 'air'.
